items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Investigating the spatial organisation of Neanderthal sites offers critical insights into their behavioural patterns, adaptive strategies, and site use. Studying how different lithic tools are organised in space and linked to specific functions is therefore essential. Kůlna Cave provides evidence of multiple occupation areas characterised by distinct activity patterns, making it a particularly suitable Neanderthal site for investigating spatial organisation and testing related hypotheses. Previous interpretations, based primarily on techno-typological analyses, proposed that the cave surface was divided into clearly defined zones for activities such as tool production, carcass processing, or serving as a “central place” for interactions. However, the actual function of tools, essential for verifying such models, remained undetermined. In our study, we applied use-wear analysis to the lithic artefacts, dated to approximately 50,000 BP (Layer 7a), to assess their function and evaluate previously proposed spatial zones. Microscopic examination of artefacts excavated between 1955–1977 focused on identifying worked materials and performed tasks, aiming to clarify the use of artefacts from different cave areas and refine interpretations of site use. The results revealed a variety of functional types and materials, correlating with distinct spatial zones. While the analysis confirmed the organised spatial structuring, it also led to a revised interpretation of functional areas, showing a more nuanced division of tasks across the cave. This research confirms that use-wear analysis is essential for evaluating spatial organisation in archaeological contexts, and it provides robust proxy data that significantly enhances interpretations of Middle Palaeolithic site use and Neanderthal behavioural complexity.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Chemical weathering plays a pivotal role in the Earth's surface material cycle and global climate regulation. It not only facilitates the reconstruction of palaeoclimate characteristics but also provides essential insights into Earth's evolutionary history. The Rb/Sr ratio has been widely applied in studies of chemical weathering and palaeoclimate reconstruction. However, its effectiveness and applicability remain limited. This study focuses on five typical terrestrial sedimentary profiles in Northeast China. By comparing the Rb/Sr ratio with the commonly used chemical weathering indices (e.g. CIA, CIW, PIA, CPA, CIX, β, Na/K and K/Al ratios), and integrating element migration characteristics and sedimentological features, we evaluate the potential of the Rb/Sr ratio to signify the degree of chemical weathering. Our findings reveal that the applicability of the Rb/Sr ratio is stage‐dependent: effective under weak‐to‐moderate weathering, limited by depositional or pedogenic overprinting, and breaks down under extreme weathering as Rb becomes mobile. Within systems characterized by stable provenance and dominated by silicate weathering, this ratio can effectively trace relative variations in chemical weathering intensity, such as the fluvial sandy gravel profile and the granite weathering profile. However, their absolute values are constrained by parent rock composition, hindering quantitative cross‐sectional comparisons. In specific depositional environments, these ratios, such as in the palaeosol profiles, deviate from the true silicate weathering progression due to influences from preferential carbonate leaching during the initial weathering stages or dynamic provenance inputs under gleyed pedogenic conditions. Crucially, a threshold effect governs the Rb/Sr ratio. In profiles subjected to extreme‐intensity chemical weathering, such as the continental red bed profile (CIA > 85), the geochemical behaviour of Rb transitions from an immobile to a mobile state. This shift results in the Rb/Sr ratio losing its indicative significance. Consequently, when applying the Rb/Sr ratio for palaeoenvironmental reconstruction, a prior assessment of its geochemical controlling mechanisms is imperative. A multi‐proxy framework must be employed for cross‐validation to ensure the scientific rigour and reliability of interpretations.</jats:p>
authors: Zhenyu Wei, Yuanyun Xie, Jie Meng, Lei Sun, Chunguo Kang, Yunping Chi, Peng Wu, Haijin Liu, Ruonan Liu, Ruitong Chang

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We use a reverse engineering approach to develop a linear programming model for the behavioural ecology of early hominins (australopithecines).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our models are based on a recently developed family of empirical models that use climate to predict how animals allocate time to core activities and, from this, whether or not they can balance their activity budget at a specific location as a guide to whether they could survive there. We first use models developed for baboons and chimpanzees to predict whether australopithecines could have survived at sites where they are known to have been present, had they been ecological baboons or ecological chimpanzees. We show that none of the hominins behaved ecologically like either baboons or chimpanzees: the models for these genera fail to predict their known distribution. We then use the equations from the baboon and chimpanzee models to build a model that predicts the known distribution of the australopithecines more precisely.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The results suggest that they had evolved their own distinctive response to environmental parameters that seems to be related to exploiting a habitat (lacustrine and riverine flood plains) that no other living primate exploits. Our analysis suggests that, in exploiting open flood plain habitats, australopithecines likely foraged as a single group for protection against predators rather than living in fission-fusion communities like modern chimpanzees. The models indicate that climate change post 2.4 Ma resulted in declining group sizes leading to eventual extinction, associated with the appearance of early
                      <jats:italic>Homo</jats:italic>
                      with novel adaptations for coping with a warmer, drier climate.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our analyses suggest that exploiting quantitative models can offer novel insights into the behavioural biology of extinct species, thereby providing rich insights into the forces that drove evolution within particular lineages.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract: Human biological and cultural evolution are tightly intertwined; the two display dependent relationships and each influences the trajectory of the other. Archaeological evidence for hominin culture first emerges ca 3.3 million years ago, but increasing data attests to an earlier, deeply rooted onset of gene-culture co-evolution in our lineage. Diverse phenotypic traits are linked to Stone Age culture via the latter's impact on the survival and success of early human populations. Hominin cognitive and language capabilities, along with the anatomy of the hand, are key examples. Similarly, variation in Stone Age culture can be linked to the biological traits of the populations from which it derives; important examples concern stone technologies, hunting strategies and social organization. The co-evolution of hominins and Stone Age culture is, therefore, complex, multi-factorial and one of the major stories in human origins research. Here, current understanding of hominin cultural and biological co-evolution prior to the advent of agriculture is reviewed, and new links between the fossil and archaeological records are drawn.

items.abstract: Rainfall magnitude and seasonality are primary determinants of African savannas today, governing essential aspects of biomass production, such as primary productivity and the amount of tree cover. It remains unclear to what extent past seasonality differed from today, potentially accounting for differences in habitats and faunal diversity. Stable isotopes along with trace elements of the growth layers in bivalve shells provide valuable insights into paleoenvironmental conditions, including rainfall, river productivity, and water temperature. In this study, we analyzed stable oxygen and carbon isotopes in 11 fossil and three modern Etheria elliptica shells collected from the middle Atbara River in eastern Sudan. The fossil specimens are from sediments dated by optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) to between ∼ 224 and ∼ 17 ka in age. The δ 18 O values of fossil and modern shells are broadly similar, although the fossils are more enriched (−2.4 ‰ to 5.9 ‰ for fossils vs. −6.4 ‰ to 1.5 ‰ for modern shells), possibly indicating more evaporative and drier conditions during the Pleistocene. However, the Atbara River is today altered by dams, which might also explain the more depleted isotopic values in modern shells. δ 13 C values are broadly similar in fossil and modern shells, ranging from −14.1 ‰ to 4.5 ‰ in fossils and −16.9 ‰ to −9.6 ‰ in modern shells but show significant changes over time. Enriched δ 13 C values in Pleistocene shells may reflect lower atmospheric CO 2 levels, while depleted values in modern shells align with post-industrial increases in CO 2 , although changes in catchment vegetation, weathering processes, or biological factors might also play a role. We also reconstructed the Atbara local meteoric water line (ALMWL) from seven river water samples. Results suggested that the Atbara River experiences low relative humidity compared to the global MWL. Moisture sources inferred from the ALMWL likely include the Indian Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, and recycled moisture from continental input. These may have also supplied moisture during the Pleistocene, as fossil and modern shells exhibit comparable isotopic ranges. Our results overall indicate that a strong precipitation seasonality pattern has likely persisted in eastern Sudan since at least ∼ 200 ka.

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The avian retina presents an elegant and highly accessible model for investigating the spatial and temporal dynamics of neurogenesis within the central nervous system. In recent years, the microtubule cytoskeleton has emerged not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a dynamic regulator of the transition of a morphologically homogeneous pool of multipotent progenitor cells to postmitotic neurons. Doublecortin (DCX) is a microtubule‐associated protein broadly recognized for its fundamental roles in neuronal migration, differentiation, and structural plasticity within the developing nervous system. While its roles in the brain are well‐documented, the precise spatiotemporal distribution of DCX in the developing retina of birds remains poorly understood. In this study we investigated the expression pattern of DCX during embryonic development of the retina of one altricial (zebra finch,
                    <jats:italic>Taeniopygia guttata</jats:italic>
                    ) and two precocial (chicken,
                    <jats:italic>Gallus gallus</jats:italic>
                    ; Japanese quail,
                    <jats:italic>Coturnix coturnix</jats:italic>
                    ) bird species using immunohistochemical techniques. Our results demonstrated that the onset of DCX expression coincided chronotopographically with the onset of neurogenesis in the developing retina. In these early stages, DCX expression is tightly colocalized with the neuronal marker class III β‐tubulin. As retinal histogenesis progressed to more advanced stages, DCX expression persisted and segregated into specific subsets of ganglion, amacrine, and horizontal cells. Furthermore, prominent immunoreactivity was maintained within the ciliary marginal zone (CMZ), highlighting its association with late‐stage retinal progenitors and ongoing neurogenesis. These findings reveal a conserved spatiotemporal expression pattern of DCX across diverse avian species. Furthermore, it suggests that some elements of the cytoskeleton and its associated regulatory proteins form a functional continuous biological continuum: first acting as drivers of neurogenesis and migration and, subsequently, transitioning into structural stabilizers that lock in and maintain the complex morphology of fully differentiated, mature retinal neurons.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Javier Francisco‐Morcillo, José Antonio de Mera‐Rodríguez, Violeta Calle‐Guisado, Gervasio Martín‐Partido, Joaquín Rodríguez‐León, Guadalupe Álvarez‐Hernán

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Brasileodactylus araripensis</jats:italic>
                    Kellner, 1984, is a toothed pterosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin, Brazil. Traditionally regarded as crestless, the species has been central to debates on anhanguerid taxonomy, as most members of the clade possess well‐developed sagittal cranial or dentary crests. Here we describe a nearly complete lower jaw (MCT.R.1473) that reveals, for the first time, the presence of a sagittal dentary crest in
                    <jats:italic>Brasileodactylus araripensis</jats:italic>
                    . The specimen was examined through high‐resolution computed tomography and incorporated into the most comprehensive phylogenetic dataset for Pterosauria, which recovered it within Anhanguerinae in close association with
                    <jats:italic>Brasileodactylus</jats:italic>
                    Kellner, 1984. The new specimen shares many diagnostic features of the taxon, including accessory sulci, paired occlusal foramina, and a sharp odontoid process, confirming its referral. Comparative data indicate that crested individuals of
                    <jats:italic>Brasileodactylus</jats:italic>
                    represent the largest known specimens of the taxon, tentatively suggesting that crest development occurred late in ontogeny (potentially following a size‐related pattern, as seen in other anhanguerids) and was possibly influenced by sexual dimorphism. The discovery of a crested
                    <jats:italic>Brasileodactylus araripensis</jats:italic>
                    challenges the assumption that crest absence can be used as a diagnostic feature, reinforcing the role of ontogeny and sexual selection in shaping pterosaur cranial morphology and underscoring the need for caution in taxonomy based primarily on crest variation.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Anderson da Silva Nascimento, Rubi Vargas Pêgas, Alessandra Silveira Machado, Ricardo Tadeu Lopes, Fabiana Rodrigues Costa
items.summary: 《巴西翼龙下颌冠首次证据及其对翼龙头冠的评述》：研究描述了巴西阿拉里皮盆地早白垩世罗穆阿尔多组一具近乎完整的下颌标本，通过高分辨率CT和系统发育分析，首次发现此前被认为无冠的阿拉里皮巴西翼龙具有矢状齿骨冠，并探讨冠的发育可能与个体发育后期及性双态有关。该发现挑战了以冠缺失作为鉴定特征的假设，值得古生物学与翼龙演化研究者阅读。
items.title: First evidence of a mandibular crest in Brasileodactylus Kellner, 1984 (Pterosauria, Pteranodontoidea, Anhangueridae), with comments on pterosaur headcrests

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Anuran limbs offer a valuable model for exploring how selective pressures, developmental constraints, and morphological evolution interact. While previous research has largely focused on total limb length, little is known about ontogenetic changes in the proportions of individual limb bones. This study introduces a novel approach using morphofunctional indices to investigate the functional roles of frog limbs, linking morphology to habitat use and locomotion. We present morphological and ontogenetic data from anurans in northwestern Argentina, emphasizing functionally relevant bone indices. Measurements were taken of 18 long bone dimensions (humerus, radioulna, femur, tibiofibula, tarsals) across 79 specimens at metamorphic, juvenile, and adult stages. Eight morphofunctional indices were calculated, including five newly proposed ones. Indices such as radioulna robustness, groove position, femur and tibiofibula robustness, and tarsal fusion differed among ecological and locomotor groups. Terrestrial hopper‐walkers such as
                    <jats:italic>Rhinella arenarum</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Rhinella spinulosa</jats:italic>
                    have more robust hind limb bones and shorter, less‐fused tarsals than jumpers like
                    <jats:italic>Boana riojana</jats:italic>
                    . These traits may be functionally associated with short‐distance jumping and shock absorption. We also observed a slenderness–robustness gradient across species, reflecting locomotor strategies. Stylopodial elements show negative allometry, while zeugopodial elements exhibit positive allometry, indicating increased precision and flexibility in limb function throughout development.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Mónica C. Soliz, María J. Tulli
items.summary: 《青蛙四肢长骨的形态功能指数与个体发育》：研究以阿根廷西北部蛙类为对象，测量变态期、幼体和成体共79件标本的18项长骨尺寸，计算8项形态功能指数，比较不同生态与运动类群间肱骨、桡尺骨、股骨、胫腓骨及跗骨的差异，并分析异速生长格局；适合关注蛙类肢体形态、运动方式与发育演化关系的读者阅读。
items.title: Morphofunctional indices and ontogeny of long bones of the limbs in the frogs

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We report the first record of a silesaurid based on an incomplete skull and articulated mandible recovered from the Upper Triassic Tiki Formation of India. The new taxon,
                    <jats:italic>Rewasaurus minori</jats:italic>
                    gen et sp. nov., is distinguished from other silesaurids by a unique combination of craniodental features, including five premaxillary teeth, of which three anterior teeth are procumbent and cylindrical, upper dentition proportionally shorter than the lower dentition, and an anterior dentary tip positioned nearly in the same plane with the remainder alveolar margin. Additionally, two isolated partial femora were recovered from the same stratigraphic horizon though from a different fossil locality. Our comprehensive phylogenetic analyses based on two different data matrices recovered
                    <jats:italic>Rewasaurus</jats:italic>
                    as either having a polytomous relationship within the monophyletic clade Silesauridae or as an early‐diverging sulcimentisaurian ornithischian having a sister–taxon relationship with
                    <jats:italic>Diodorus scytobrachion</jats:italic>
                    . Although the isolated femora are recovered as a silesaurid, the absence of overlapping skeletal elements precludes a confident assignment to
                    <jats:italic>Rewasaurus</jats:italic>
                    . A grasping feeding apparatus adapted for exploiting easily processed soft‐bodied preys and plant material available in the Tiki floodplains is suggested for
                    <jats:italic>Rewasaurus</jats:italic>
                    . A time‐calibrated phylogenetic tree suggests that the silesaurids underwent two major diversification phases and dispersed eastward and northward, with the former commencing considerably later. The notable scarcity of silesaurids and/or unambiguous ornithischians during the Rhaetian may be associated with global environmental perturbation across the Norian–Rhaetian Boundary.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《印度上三叠统首次确证的西里龙类（鸟跖类：恐龙形类）记录及其起源与扩散的新见解》：研究报道了印度蒂基组一件不完整头骨及关联下颌，命名新属种Rewasaurus minori，并基于系统发育分析探讨西里龙类的演化关系、两次主要多样化阶段及扩散方向，还提出其取食适应与诺利期—瑞替期界线环境扰动相关的推测，适合关注三叠纪恐龙形类演化与古地理扩散的读者阅读。
